test.title: Motion in One Dimension - Test 1
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text: A body travels $102.5 \mathrm{~m}$ in $\mathrm{n}^{\text {th }}$ second and $115.0 \mathrm{~m}$ in $(\mathrm{n}+2)^{\text {th }}$ second. The acceleration is :

A particle starts with an initial velocity of 10.0 ms-1 along x-direction and accelerates uniformly at the rate of 2.0 m s-2. The time taken by the particle to reach the velocity of 60.0 m s-1 is _____.

An object of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is thrown vertically upwards from the ground. The air resistance produces a constant retarding force of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> throughout the motion. The ratio of time of ascent to the time of descent will be equal to : [Use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>].
The velocity-time graph of an object moving along a straight line is shown in figure. What is the distance covered by the object between $t=0$ to $t=4 \mathrm{~s}$ ?

The position co-ordinates of a particle moving in a 3D coordinate system is given by

x=acos⁡ωt

y=asin⁡ωt

and z=aωt

The speed of the particle is:

Train <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> and train <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> are running on parallel tracks in the opposite directions with speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>36</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>hour</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>72</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>hour</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, respectively. A person is walking in train <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> in the direction opposite to its motion with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi>km</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi>hour</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>in</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math> of this person as observed from train <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> will be close to: (take the distance between the tracks as negligible)

The velocity of a particle is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>F</mi><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Its position is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mo>;</mo></math> then its displacement after time <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mo>)</mo></math> is :

Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Area under velocity-time graph gives the distance travelled by the body in a given time.
Statement II: Area under acceleration-time graph is equal to the change in velocity in the given time.
In the light of given statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true

question.text: A small ball of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is thrown upward with velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi></math> from the ground. The ball experiences a resistive force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi><mi>k</mi><msup><mi>v</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi></math> is it speed. The maximum height attained by the ball is :
A person is standing in an elevator. In which situation, he experiences weight loss ?

options.text: When the elevator moves upward with constant acceleration
When the elevator moves downward with constant acceleration
When the elevator moves upward with uniform velocity
When the elevator moves downward with uniform velocity

question.text: A bullet is fired into a fixed target looses one third of its velocity after travelling <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. It penetrates further <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>D</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> before coming to rest. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>D</mi></math> is :

Two trains A and B of length l and 4l are travelling into a tunnel of length L in parallel tracks from opposite directions with velocities 108 km h-1 and 72 km h-1, respectively. If train A take 35 s less time than train B to cross the tunnel then, length L of tunnel is:

(Given L=60 l)

An engine of a train, moving with uniform acceleration, passes the signal-post with velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>u</mi></math> and the last compartment with velocity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi></math>. The velocity with which middle point of the train passes the signal post is :

A particle starts from origin O from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration along the positive  x-axis . Identify all figures that correctly represent the motion qualitatively.
( a= acceleration, v= velocity, x=  dispalcement, t= time)
A
B
(C)
(D)

A helicopter flying horizontally with a speed of $360 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ at an altitude of 2 km , drops an object at an instant. The object hits the ground at a point O , 20 s after it is dropped. Displacement of ' O ' from the position of helicopter where the object was released is :
(use acceleration due to gravity $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ and neglect air resistance)

A stone is dropped from the top of a building. When it crosses a point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> below the top, another stone starts to fall from a point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> below the top. Both stones reach the bottom of building simultaneously. The height of the building is :

A body of mass 2 kg moving with velocity of $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_{\mathrm{in}}=3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+4 \hat{\mathrm{j}} \mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ enters into a constant force field of 6 N directed along positive z -axis. If the body remains in the field for a period of $\frac{5}{3}$ seconds, then velocity of the body when it emerges from force field is

Two cars are travelling towards each other at speed of $20 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$ each. When the cars are $300 \mathrm{~m}$ apart, both the drivers apply brakes and the cars retard at the rate of $2 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}$. The distance between them when they come to rest is :

A particle is moving unidirectional on a horizontal plane under the action of a constant power supplying energy source. The displacement (s) – time (t) graph that describes the motion of the particle is (graphs are drawn schematically and are not to scale):

A car travels a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> with speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and then same distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> with speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> in the same direction. The average speed of the car is:

A car covers AB distance with first one-third at velocity v1 m s-1, second one-third at v2 m s-1 and last one-third at v3 m s-1. If v3=3v1,v2=2v1 and v1=11 m s-1, then the average velocity of the car is _____  m s-1.

If the velocity of a body related to displacement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mn>5000</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>24</mn><mi>x</mi></msqrt><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></math> then the acceleration of the body is _________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math>

A tennis ball is dropped on to the floor from a height of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. It rebounds to a height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. Ball comes in contact with the floor for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The average acceleration during contact is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. [Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>]
The speed versus time graph for a particle is shown in the figure. The distance travelled (in m) by the particle during the time interval t=0 to t=5 s will be __________

A body moves on a frictionless plane starting from rest. If $S_n$ is distance moved between $t=n-1$ and $\mathrm{t}=\mathrm{n}$ and $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{n}-1}$ is distance moved between $\mathrm{t}=\mathrm{n}-2$ and $\mathrm{t}=\mathrm{n}-1$, then the ratio $\frac{\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{n}-1}}{\mathrm{~S}_{\mathrm{n}}}$ is $\left(1-\frac{2}{x}\right)$ for $\mathrm{n}=10$. The value of $x$ is ______.
